headline: Readiness is red (33.6/100, HRV-driven) but not a crash — the battery recovered well overnight, so today's scheduled 7km easy run stays exactly that: easy, no swap needed.
body_state: Readiness composite reads **33.6/100, red band**, HRV the driver: Garmin's own training_readiness sits at 36, HRV last night was 36ms below your usual range (Garmin still labels it BALANCED, but the composite's own trend disagrees), and 14-day sleep debt has built to ~25h despite a decent night (7.9h, sleep score 70). Body battery recovered well overnight though — +45 points to **46** this morning, so the tank isn't empty. Garmin status reads "Recovery." On the training-load side TSB is **-17.2** (CTL 37.4), still inside the -5 to -30 productive-building band — this is a recovery-signal day, not an overreaching one, and the plan already prescribes the right response.
session: Today is the **7km Easy Run, 4:51–5:20/km** — no edit needed, the schedule already matches the readiness call. Run the slow end of that band, HR held well under your 163 lactate-threshold (ideally zone 1-2). Wednesday's (8/12) tempo showed what "easy creep" costs: HR stayed 20bpm under threshold despite RPE 8, a fatigue flag, not a fitness one. Keep today honestly easy so it actually recovers something.
recent: Wed 8/12's scheduled tempo came up short — 5.43 of 7km (78%, yellow), tempo pace 4:38/km vs the 4:18–4:32 target, HR topping just 156 against your 163 threshold despite RPE 8: hard-feeling but not physiologically hard, and cutting it short was the right call. focus: Hold today's run at 5:00+/km, HR zone 1-2 — no grey-zone creep
